ship of magic.title: Ship of Magic
ship of magic.author: Robin Hobb
ship of magic.why: First of the Liveship Traders, about living ships and a merchant family; readers are caught by the concept though the start is slow.

book of dave.title: The Book of Dave
book of dave.author: Will Self
book of dave.why: A bitter London cabbie's writings become the holy book of a far-future society; a bold, dialect-heavy satire.

blood and guts in high school.title: Blood and Guts in High School
blood and guts in high school.author: Kathy Acker
blood and guts in high school.why: A transgressive, experimental novel of a girl's life in New York and beyond; a cult feminist avant-garde book.

sweetness at the bottom of the pie.title: The Sweetness at the Bottom of the Pie
sweetness at the bottom of the pie.author: Alan Bradley
sweetness at the bottom of the pie.why: An eleven-year-old chemist in 1950s England solves a murder; charming cozy mystery.

debt to pleasure.title: The Debt to Pleasure
debt to pleasure.author: John Lanchester
debt to pleasure.why: A witty, unreliable narrator tells his life through food and recipes; a darkly comic gem.

wizards first rule.title: Wizard's First Rule
wizards first rule.author: Terry Goodkind
wizards first rule.why: A woodsman and a mysterious woman are hunted in the first book of the Sword of Truth; a long, fast-paced fantasy.

uglies.title: Uglies
uglies.author: Scott Westerfeld
uglies.why: In a world where everyone gets pretty surgery at sixteen, a girl discovers what is hidden; an easy YA dystopia that readers found meaningful.

outline.title: Outline
outline.author: Rachel Cusk
outline.why: A writer in Athens listens to the stories others tell her; a spare, unusual novel that fans of literary fiction recommend.

nos4a2.title: NOS4A2
nos4a2.author: Joe Hill
nos4a2.why: A woman fights a vampiric man who takes children to Christmasland; a perfect holiday-season horror read.

lost apothecary.title: The Lost Apothecary
lost apothecary.author: Sarah Penner
lost apothecary.why: A London apothecary who sells poisons to women and a modern woman who uncovers her story; an atmospheric, easy read.

kind worth killing.title: The Kind Worth Killing
kind worth killing.author: Peter Swanson
kind worth killing.why: A chance meeting on a plane leads to a plot to kill; a twisty thriller with a big surprise.

orchard keeper.title: The Orchard Keeper
orchard keeper.author: Cormac McCarthy
orchard keeper.why: McCarthy's debut about a boy, an old man and an outlaw in the Tennessee mountains; lyrical and bleak.

rabbit hutch.title: The Rabbit Hutch
rabbit hutch.author: Tess Gunty
rabbit hutch.why: The residents of a decaying apartment block in Indiana in a dazzling, strange novel.

far from the tree.title: Far From the Tree
far from the tree.author: Andrew Solomon
far from the tree.why: A study of families raising children very different from them, through interviews; thought-provoking and moving.

billy summers.title: Billy Summers
billy summers.author: Stephen King
billy summers.why: A hitman with a conscience takes one last job and writes his story; a surprising, gripping King thriller.

sea wolf.title: The Sea-Wolf
sea wolf.author: Jack London
sea wolf.why: A literary man is rescued by the brutal captain of a sealing ship; a stirring sea adventure.

black sun.title: Black Sun
black sun.author: Rebecca Roanhorse
black sun.why: A Mesoamerican-inspired fantasy of a ship, a prophecy and a sun-priest; readers enjoyed it greatly.

necklace.title: The Necklace
necklace.author: Guy de Maupassant
necklace.why: A woman loses a borrowed necklace and ruins her life paying for it; a short story with a famous twist.

nestlings.title: Nestlings
nestlings.author: Nat Cassidy
nestlings.why: A horror about a family in a haunted apartment, but opinions are split and one reader calls it a waste of time.

two years before the mast.title: Two Years Before the Mast
two years before the mast.author: Richard Henry Dana Jr.
two years before the mast.why: A Harvard student's memoir of life as a common sailor in 1830s California; a seafaring classic.

egyptian.title: The Egyptian
egyptian.author: Mika Waltari
egyptian.why: A physician's life in the Egypt of Akhenaten, told with detail and cynicism; a historical epic.

silence of the girls.title: The Silence of the Girls
silence of the girls.author: Pat Barker
silence of the girls.why: The Trojan War told from the perspective of Briseis, a captive woman; a powerful retelling.

king of elflands daughter.title: The King of Elfland's Daughter
king of elflands daughter.author: Lord Dunsany
king of elflands daughter.why: A lyrical, early fantasy about a prince who marries an elf princess; a clear inspiration for Tolkien.

vampire chronicles.title: The Vampire Chronicles
vampire chronicles.author: Anne Rice
vampire chronicles.why: Lestat and other vampires through centuries, starting with Interview with the Vampire; a queer, gothic series that shaped modern vampire fiction.
